# KitchenSink4PPT

> Everything plus the kitchen sink for Microsoft PowerPoint: the KitchenSink-family .pptx MCP server. 9 tools with 145 operations between them (193 counting each action), about 7.3k tokens at startup, everything available from the first call. Headline capability: native tweakable graphics, meaning SVG converted to grouped native PowerPoint shapes with glued connectors, editable afterward by shape identity (move the node, the arrows follow). Also file-based structural table operations (merge cells, insert and delete rows and columns), slide operations done right (insert, deep duplicate, delete with cleanup, reorder, hide), create-from-template with theme-color-referenced fills, and render-to-verify export. Engineered not to corrupt: atomic validated saves, automatic backups before every mutation, byte-identical passthrough of untouched parts. Ambiguous targets are refused with every candidate listed instead of guessed.

Release: v2.0.0
Platform: file-based tools (the large majority) run on Windows and Linux (macOS is untested in this release) and need no PowerPoint installation; the export and validation tools (PDF, per-slide PNG, opens-clean check) use a local Microsoft PowerPoint via COM on Windows when present.
MCP transport: stdio.

## Install

- pip: `pip install kitchensink4ppt`
- uvx (no install): `uvx kitchensink4ppt`
- Claude Desktop: download the `.mcpb` bundle from the latest GitHub release and open it. Requires `uv` on PATH.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add ppt -s user -- uvx kitchensink4ppt`
- Codex CLI: `codex mcp add ppt -- uvx kitchensink4ppt`
- Any other MCP client: run the `kitchensink4ppt` (or `ppt-mcp`) executable over stdio, e.g. `{"mcpServers": {"ppt": {"command": "kitchensink4ppt"}}}`
- MCP registry name: `io.github.KitchenSink4AI/kitchensink4ppt`

## How the surface works (new in 2.0)

The server offers nine tools. Every tool except `ppt_help` takes `{op, args}`: `op` names the operation and `args` holds its arguments, including `file_path` (the .pptx) unless the operation names other paths. Call `ppt_help` with an `op` to get that operation's arguments and a validated example. Unknown arguments are refused by name. A few names a model reaches for first are read as the operation's own: `shape_id` as `shape`, `font_size` as `size_pt` (or `size` on the placeholder operations), and `slides` as `scope` on the scoped operations; the answer's `normalized_from` says which name was read as which, and two names sent with different values are refused. Slides: `slide` counts from 0 and `slide_number` counts from 1, so the slide a user calls slide 2 is `slide_number` 2 or `slide` 1. Every answer about one slide starts with its `slide_number`, `slide_count` and `slide_title`; `slide_count` is the deck after the call, `delete_slide` names the removed slide `deleted_slide_number`, and `duplicate_slide` and `copy_slide_between` name the copied slide `source_slide_number`. When the slide was named by `slide` or `slide_index`, a `slide_note` says in words which slide that was. A read whose `scope` names one slide starts the same way, and `slide_count` always counts the whole deck; a scoped read adds `slides_in_scope`. The other arguments that name slides or positions (`to_slide`, `to`, `position`, `order`, `slides`, `scope`) count from 0, like `slide`, and `ppt_help` describes each one. Each has a twin counted from 1, such as `to_slide_number`, `to_number`, `position_number`, `order_numbers`, `number_ranges` and `slide_numbers`, except the `scope` of `set_footer`, whose own `slide_number` turns slide numbers on; send one form, not both. A change whose answer passes the output limit is shortened, never refused, and `page.note` says the change stands. All 145 operations are available from the start; there is nothing to enable and no tool-set switching. About 7,316 approximate tokens cover the whole surface.

- `ppt_read` (18 operations): read without changing anything. `get_presentation_view` (anchored markdown projection of the deck: slides, shapes with ids, tables, notes), `get_slide_info`, `get_text`, `find_text` (deck-wide, or in a `scope` of slides, a range such as `{"start": 1, "end": 3}` or `slide_numbers` counted from 1; exact case unless `match_case` is false, and `case_note` says where matches in another case are), `extract_text`, `list_elements`, `list_hyperlinks` (links and click actions on shapes, text, table cells, notes, SmartArt, layouts and masters, with broken ones flagged), `get_table`, `get_chart_data`, `get_notes`, `list_comments`, `list_equations`, `get_transitions`, `list_animations`, `get_server_info` (the authoritative runtime identity record: product, edition, version, test count, tool surface), `get_workflows`.
- `ppt_inspect` (17 operations): audits that change nothing. `audit_accessibility`, `check_layout`, `font_inventory`, `comment_report`, `compare_decks`, `deck_statistics`, `diagnose`, `extract_brand`, `get_theme`, `get_autofit_state`, `get_document_properties`, `get_export_engines`, `live_status`, `powerpoint_status`, `zombie_check`.
- `ppt_edit` (19 operations): text, notes and slides. `apply_edits` (batched, every anchor validated first, one backup and one save per batch; it batches speaker notes too), `search_and_replace`, `set_placeholder_text`, `fit_text`, `format_text`, `set_bullets`, `insert_textbox`, `set_notes` (one slide, or many slides in one save with `notes`, each entry named by `slide_id` or `slide_number`), `set_hyperlink`, `insert_slide`, `delete_slide`, `duplicate_slide`, `reorder_slides`, `move_slide`, `set_slide_hidden`, `manage_section`, `set_language`.
- `ppt_graphics` (27 operations, the centerpiece): `svg_to_shapes` (arbitrary SVG compiled to grouped native PowerPoint shapes; transforms flattened, arcs converted to Beziers), `insert_shape` (presets plus freeform custom geometry, gradients, theme-color fills), `insert_connector` (straight, elbow, curved, GLUED to shapes so they follow when a shape moves), `set_shape` (edit in place by shape id, name or group path; with a resize it can scale text and line widths), `set_shape_adjustments` (read and set a preset shape's adjust handles by name, angles in degrees), `copy_shape_between` (a shape or group from a slide of another deck, with its pictures, charts and links), `generate_diagram` (timeline, org chart, matrix, cycle, comparison in one call), `group_shapes`, `ungroup_shapes`, `align_shapes`, `distribute_shapes`, `set_z_order`, images, video, audio, equations, `set_alt_text`, `set_reading_order`.
- `ppt_tables` (16 operations): `create_table`, `set_table_cells`, `merge_cells`, `unmerge_cells`, insert and delete rows AND columns, `format_table_cells`, `set_column_widths`, `set_row_heights`, `apply_table_style`, `import_table`, and charts (`create_chart`, `update_chart_data`, `format_chart`) with editable data workbooks.
- `ppt_design` (19 operations): `set_slide_size`, `apply_layout`, `set_theme_colors`, `set_theme_fonts`, `apply_brand`, backgrounds, master and layout editing (`create_layout`, placeholders, decoration shapes), `replace_fonts`, `replace_colors`, `set_transition`, `add_entrance_animation`, `clear_animations`.
- `ppt_review` (7 operations): threaded comments (`add_comment`, `reply_to_comment`, `resolve_comment`, `delete_comment`) and `anonymize_deck`; also `update_now` (updates the server, only when the user asks or agrees) and `update_notices` (turns update notices on, off, or reports their status).
- `ppt_deck` (22 operations): `create_presentation` (from YOUR template), `copy_presentation`, `create_snapshot` (a permanent copy, kept in the deck's hidden backup folder unless `dest_dir` names a folder for a visible one), `manage_backups`, `copy_slide_between`, `merge_decks`, `split_deck`, `export_pdf` (COM), `export_slide_image` (per-slide PNG, the render-to-verify primitive), `export_shape_image` (one shape or group as a PNG), `export_handout`, `export_table`, `generate_agenda_slide`, `refresh_agenda_slide`, `set_footer`, `compress_deck`, `validate` (opens-clean plus overflow report), `live_save`, `live_scroll_to`.
- `ppt_help`: the arguments and an example for any operation.

The operations figure is produced by `scripts/measure_surface.py` (145 over real stdio). The figure that counts each action separately, 193, is produced by `scripts/count_operations.py`, which reads the dispatch values each operation actually validates out of committed source. Its docstring carries the counting definition and the exclusions.

Launch settings can narrow the surface. `KS4P_READ_ONLY=1` leaves only `ppt_read`, `ppt_inspect` and `ppt_help`. `KS4P_FORBID` removes named tools or operations (`ppt_app`, which is not one of the nine tools, is also accepted as a name and removes everything that starts or attaches to PowerPoint). `KS4P_ALLOWED_ROOTS` sandboxes every path. `KS4P_CALL_TIMEOUT_S` and `KS4P_MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS` bound a call's time and reply size. `KS4P_AUTHOR` chooses who signs a comment or reply whose call names no author: `user` (the default: the user's own name, their Office user name or Windows sign-in name) or `assistant` ("AI Assistant via KS4PPT", which a call also gets with `author="assistant"`); `KS4P_COMMENT_AUTHOR` names one outright, and the answer's `author_source` says which applied. An email address never signs, whether a setting names it or a call sends it as `author`: the next choice signs and the answer says so. `KS4P_UPDATE_CHECK=off` disables the weekly version check completely, and `KS4P_UPDATE_NOTICES=off` turns the update notices off and keeps the check (`on` turns them back on). Update notices: at most once a week, after a tool call, the server asks PyPI in the background which version is newest; the request names only the package and the installed version. When a newer version exists, a client with form elicitation shows a dialog (Update now / Not now) after a read when the server runs from uvx or the Claude Desktop bundle; otherwise a read result gets one `update` field, to relay once. `ppt_review` `update_now` installs the new version only when the user asks or agrees, and `update_notices` (`on`, `off`, `status`) changes the setting from any client. It never downloads or installs a new version unless the user chooses Update now in its notice or asks the AI to update it. The 1.x settings `KS4P_MODE`, `KS4P_PACK_POLICY`, `KS4P_ALL_TOOLS` and `KS4P_LOCK_TOOLS` are retired. Settings from earlier versions are handled for you: an old default (`KS4P_MODE=lite`, `full` or `everything`, `KS4P_PACK_POLICY=auto`, `KS4P_ALL_TOOLS`, `KS4P_LOCK_TOOLS=false`) is ignored with a one-line notice, and a setting that locked the tools (`KS4P_PACK_POLICY=locked`, `KS4P_LOCK_TOOLS=true` or a `KS4P_MODE` list of tool groups) stops the start with a message naming what to use instead. A call refused because of a launch setting returns `NOT_AVAILABLE`, and no tool call can undo it.

Do not infer product facts from remembered documentation. `get_server_info` is the authoritative record.

## Upgrading from 1.x

Version 2.0 regroups the 142 flat tools of 1.3.1 into the nine tools above. Every 1.3.1 operation survives except `enable_tools` and `disable_tools`, which are gone because nothing needs enabling. Call a former tool as an operation of the group that now holds it: `ppt_graphics` with `op: "svg_to_shapes"` replaces the tool `svg_to_shapes`. The full map is `docs/surface_map.md` in the repository, and `get_workflows` with the `migrate-from-v1` recipe returns it too. Some arguments changed; check `ppt_help` for the operation before the first call.

## Recommended workflows

`get_workflows` returns the recipes with the right tool and operation for each step. The common ones:

Build a diagram an audience member can still adjust:
`ppt_graphics svg_to_shapes` (the whole diagram lands as one grouped set of native shapes with glued connectors) -> `ppt_graphics set_shape` by id for any tweak -> `ppt_deck export_slide_image` to verify visually -> `ppt_deck validate`.

Restructure a table nobody else can touch:
`ppt_read get_presentation_view` (find the table and its anchor) -> `ppt_tables` insert or delete columns, `merge_cells`, `format_table_cells` -> `set_table_cells` for the data -> `ppt_deck validate`.

Build a deck on the house template:
`ppt_deck create_presentation` from the template -> `ppt_design apply_layout` per slide -> populate placeholders with `ppt_edit set_placeholder_text` -> theme-color fills for any added shapes -> `ppt_deck export_pdf`.

Heavy editing with a safety net:
`ppt_deck copy_presentation` (work on a copy) -> `ppt_deck create_snapshot` -> `ppt_read get_presentation_view` -> `ppt_edit apply_edits` (batched, anchors validated) -> `ppt_deck validate` -> `ppt_deck export_slide_image` on changed slides.

Use `refresh-an-existing-deck` when updating an established presentation rather than rebuilding it as a new deck.

## Result contracts

Every read is bounded. When a result is incomplete, the response says so and supplies the continuation needed to retrieve the next page. Treat `page`, `returned`, and any continuation field as part of the result contract. Never infer that `slide_count` items were returned merely because the presentation contains that many slides. Continue until the response says no content remains. Long answers start with their totals and paging details, so a client that shows only the start of an answer still sees how much there is. `extract_text` accepts `limit` and `offset`; `check_layout` accepts `min_group_overlap_in` and `exclude_names`.

A contrast result can be informational when the background cannot be reduced to one dependable color, including pictures, gradients and PowerPoint built-in table styles. Do not turn an undetermined result into a pass or an error.

`create_presentation(slide_size=...)` accepts only the presets listed in its description. It refuses an unknown value and refuses `slide_size` when a template is also supplied. A presentation created without a template defaults to 16:9; request 4:3 explicitly when required. A template keeps its own slide size, and `create_presentation` reports the sensitivity label and core properties it inherits from the template. `set_slide_size` changes the canvas without moving existing content.

After replacing text, inspect the result for the formatting that was preserved and for `autofit_scale_reset`. That note means the previous shrink value was cleared and the new fit is unknown. Do not claim that replacement text was refitted. Use `fit_text` when the text must be fitted deliberately.

`format_text` accepts `anchor` and `wrap`. Inside `apply_edits`, the vertical-anchor key is `text_anchor`, and `set_paragraph`, `insert_paragraph` and `delete_paragraph` change one paragraph of a shape, counted from 0 as `find_text` reports it (or `paragraph_number`, counted from 1), as the shape was before the batch. `set_text` replaces every paragraph: new paragraph N takes old paragraph N's formatting. `search_and_replace` with `remove_empty_paragraphs` removes the paragraphs its replacements leave empty. Unknown keys in line and fill specifications are refused by name. Bullets get a default hanging indent on text boxes; `indent: "none"` clears it, and `space_before` and `space_after` are available.

`validate` may return `failed_slide_index`, `failed_slide_id`, `failed_shape_index` and `failed_shape_name`. Its PowerPoint check gets more time on a bigger deck (slides, shapes, notes pages and media, up to 300 seconds), and `opens_clean_time_limit` says how much; a check that runs out of time answers `opens_clean: null` and `timed_out: true`, which is a time limit, not a verdict on the deck. Install `kitchensink4ppt[metrics]` for installed-font width measurement; `fit_text`, `get_autofit_state` and `check_layout` report `method="font-metrics"` or `method="estimate"`. `create_table` accepts `row_heights` and `col_widths` as a full inches list or `{index: inches}`. `KS4P_PDFTOPPM` names the poppler executable.

## Safety model

- Atomic validated saves; a failed operation leaves the original byte-identical.
- Automatic timestamped backup before every file mutation.
- Byte-identical passthrough of anything not being edited: animations, media, embedded objects, and unrecognized parts pass through untouched.
- Ambiguous targets are REFUSED with a candidate list; no tool ever acts on a first match.
- Slide order is resolved through the presentation's slide list, never ZIP entry order.
- Presentation writes are serialized across processes. A live lock is not reclaimed merely because it is more than ten minutes old, and a lock written by another host is not reclaimed locally. Wait for the lock or report the refusal.
- Only a PowerPoint process started by this server is ever ended, and a hung call is cancelled safely. A PowerPoint that was already running is left alone.
- An encrypted presentation is refused before any Office call, and a read-only file is reported as read-only.
- Saves preserve each embedded media file's existing compression. A text or structure edit must not recompress unrelated media.
- Release evidence for 2.0: a suite of 3,689 tests, including checks that generated decks open in PowerPoint and fail on any repair prompt, and a raw MCP stdio round-trip suite.

## Documented refusals

These are contracts. Handle them; do not retry blindly. The closed error codes:

- `AMBIGUOUS_LOCATION` several targets matched; use one of the addresses in the message.
- `NOT_FOUND` re-run `ppt_read get_presentation_view` or `get_slide_info` to see current slides, ids, and anchors.
- `STALE_ANCHOR` the deck changed since the view was taken; re-run `get_presentation_view` and resend with fresh anchors.
- `DOCUMENT_LOCKED` close the file in PowerPoint (or wait out the other process) and retry; operations with a live argument accept `live='auto'` to edit the open copy instead. The read operations are not refused for this: they read the file as last saved and say so in `open_deck_note`.
- `VALIDATION_FAILED` the original file was NOT modified; the message says what the produced package failed.
- `APP_NOT_RUNNING` this operation needs PowerPoint installed and reachable.
- `APP_BUSY` PowerPoint is showing a dialog or running a command; clear it and retry.
- `APP_BLOCKED` PowerPoint is not answering; wait or close the dialog.
- `PROTECTED_VIEW` click Enable Editing in PowerPoint first.
- `PROTECTED` the file is protected; remove the protection in PowerPoint, or edit the open copy live.
- `UNSUPPORTED_CONTENT` structurally unsupported, protected or damaged content, refused instead of written partially.
- `CONFLICT` the destination exists and overwrite was not requested, or PowerPoint disconnected during the call.
- `BAD_ARGS` the arguments did not fit the operation; `ppt_help` with that op gives them and an example.
- `BAD_PARAMS` the request did not fit the operation, including a path outside the configured sandbox roots (`KS4P_ALLOWED_ROOTS`).
- `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` the answer would pass the output limit; narrow the request.
- `TIMEOUT` the call ran past its limit; `details.saved` says whether anything was saved.
- `NOT_AVAILABLE` a launch setting turned this off.
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` try once more, then report it with the version from `get_server_info`.

Refusals are the reliability feature, not the failure mode. A refusal names
what was wrong, leaves the file untouched, and carries the next call in
`hint`. Retrying the same call unchanged is never the fix.

## The KitchenSink family

- KitchenSink4Word (231 actions in 115 operations across 10 tools for .docx): https://community.kitchensink4.ai/word/
- KitchenSink4XL (the electrical aisle, 131 actions in 69 operations across 7 tools for .xlsx, every value labeled calculated, cached, or absent): https://community.kitchensink4.ai/xl/
- KitchenSink4Web (the garden section, browser automation with budget-priced page reads and a consent ladder): https://community.kitchensink4.ai/web/
- Family storefront: https://community.kitchensink4.ai/
